PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-06-22
51F, outpatient visit for a routine evaluation.

S:
Patient presents for a routine outpatient visit. She reports feeling generally well, with occasional wheezing on exertion and with pollen exposure that responds to her reliever within a few minutes. No shortness of breath. Diet includes frequent sugary drinks and takeout lunches, which was discussed. She works as a school librarian and stays on her feet much of the day. Sister with schizophrenia. Appetite is good and sleep is adequate, about 7 hours a night. Lives with her spouse. Never smoker, rare alcohol.

O:
BP 120/76, HR 72, RR 14, Temp 98.1 F, SpO2 98% on room air. Weight 158 lb, BMI 26.
General: well appearing, in no acute distress.
HEENT: nasal mucosa normal, oropharynx clear.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abdomen: soft, nontender.
Extremities: no edema.
Labs (prior week): A1c 6.0%, basic metabolic panel within normal limits, lipid panel within goal.

A/P:
1. Asthma, uncomplicated, using inhaler as needed. Continue short-acting reliever before exertion; inhaler technique reviewed and adequate. Provided a written action plan and discussed avoiding known triggers.
2. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Reviewed reducing sugary drinks and adding regular walks. Recheck A1c in 6 months.
3. Family history: noted for the record and reviewed with patient; discussed reassurance and routine follow-up.
4. Health maintenance: cervical screening up to date; mammography discussed and scheduled. Influenza vaccine offered in the fall.

Return in 12 months for the next wellness visit, sooner if breathing or new symptoms develop.
